items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the county law and the executive law, in relation to the
reporting of a veteran's suicide
items.lawCode: Amd §677, County L; amd §353, Exec L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2036

SPONSOR: BROOKS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the county law and the executive law, in relation to the
reporting of a veteran's suicide

 
PURPOSE:

Requires the Division of Veterans Service to design a form that coron-
ers, coroner's physicians and medical examiners will use to report
deaths of veterans they suspect have been caused by suicide.  The report
will be provided to DVS.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. amends section 677of the County Law by adding a new subdivi-
sion 10 to direct a coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner to
report, through the use of a one page form, to the Division of Veterans'
Affairs, any death which appears to be a suicide by a person who is
believed to be a veteran.

Section 2 amends the Executive Law to add a new subdivision directing
the Division of Veterans' Affairs to develop a one page form to be used
by a coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner for reporting any
death which appears to be a suicide by a person who is believed to be a
veteran.

Section 3 establishes that the Division of Veterans' Affairs must estab-
lish and implement the procedures and forms necessary for implementation
of this act within 60 days.

Section 4 establishes an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the Pentagon's annual suicide report, active duty military
suicides hit a record high in 2018, jumping by 13%.  Additionally,
according to the 2019 National Veteran Suicide Prevention Report, the
number of veteran suicides has exceeded 6,000 each year from 2008 to
2017. In November 2017, the New York State Suicide Prevention Task Force
was created. This past April, the Task Force released a report on its
findings. Among its many findings specifically related to veterans, the
Task Force found that veteran suicide rates are significantly higher
than those rates of non-veterans. Issues with reporting data, often
inaccurate and incomplete, are a common issue in both national and state
reports. This legislation is an attempt to improve the data gathering
methods to respond with appropriate measures. If a coroner or the person
acting on his/her behalf has reason to believe there has been a suicide
by a veteran, he/she shall notify the Division of Veterans' Affairs
through the use of a simple one-page form, provided by DVS.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Nominal cost to Division of Veterans' Services.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER: S2036B

SPONSOR: BROOKS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the county law and the executive law, in relation to the
reporting of a veteran's suicide

 
PURPOSE:

Requires the Division of Veterans Service to design a form that coron-
ers, coroner's physicians and medical examiners will use to report
deaths of veterans they suspect have been caused by suicide.  The report
will be provided to DVS.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. amends section 677of the County Law by adding a new subdivi-
sion 10 to direct a coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner to
report, through the use of a one page form, to the Division of Veterans'
Services, any death which appears to be a suicide by a person who is
believed to be a veteran.

Section 2 amends the Executive Law to add a new subdivision 26 directing
the Division of Veterans' Services to develop a one page form to be used
by a coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner for reporting any
death which appears to be a suicide by a person who is believed to be a
veteran, encompassing various privacy protections therein. The section
also stipulates that the form shall be forwarded to the Office of Mental
Hygiene.

Section 3 directs the Department of Veterans' Services to create a
report in conjunction with the Office of Mental Hygiene and the Depart-
ment of Health on the data that they have collected. The report shall be
given to the Governor and the Legislature no later than June 13, 2024
and every three years after and will be posted on the department's
website as well.

Section 4 is the enacting clause.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the Pentagon's annual suicide report, active duty military
suicides hit a record high in 2018, jumping by 13%.  Additionally,
according to the 2019 National Veteran Suicide Prevention Report, the
number of veteran suicides has exceeded 6,000 each year from 2008 to
2017. In November 2017, the New York State Suicide Prevention Task Force
was created. This past April, the Task Force released a report on its
findings. Among its many findings specifically related to veterans, the
Task Force found that veteran suicide rates are significantly higher
than those rates of non-veterans. Issues with reporting data, often
inaccurate and incomplete, are a common issue in both national and state
reports. This legislation is an attempt to improve the data gathering
methods to respond with appropriate measures. If a coroner or the person
acting on his/her behalf has reason to believe there has been a suicide
by a veteran, he/she shall notify the Division of Veterans' Services
through the use of a simple one-page form, provided by DVS.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Nominal cost to Division of Veterans' Services.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect 180 days after it shall become law.  Effec-
tive immediately, the addition, or amendment and/or repeal of any rule
of regulation necessary for the implementation of this act on its effec-
tive date are authorized to be made and completed on or before such
effective date.

summary: Provides that the coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner shall promptly report to the division of veterans' services, in a form developed and provided by such division, any death which appears to be a suicide by a person who, to the knowledge of the coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner, is a veteran; a report shall be provided to the governor and legislature on certain suicide statistics no later than June 13, 2024.
